value.account:
CHANGED
- State (orchestrator/state.py): optional RunState.result_persistence_profile (omitted from to_dict when absent; ValueError naming the profile on construction, StateManager.initialize and load). initialize(..., result_persistence_profile=) writes it atomically. Added StateManager.begin_eligible_pure_visit, reuse_interrupted_eligible_pure_visit, settle_eligible_pure_success and settle_eligible_pure_failure (each via state_transaction), with the same methods on _CallFrameStateManager.
- Selection: run.py (typed .orc run) and resume.py (--force-restart new root) pass the profile. calls.py selects it only for a fresh, non-iterative child frame whose callee has provenance.frontend_kind == workflow_lisp; the decision never reads the parent's profile. call_frame_state.py: load_existing_call_frame_read_only; a malformed existing frame is rejected with 'existing call-frame state' before any directory or state write; existing frames are not backfilled.
- New modules, re-exported by orchestrator/workflow/pure_result_replay.py (split to stay under 500 lines): pure_replay_index.py (errors, constants, eligibility, index, literal type checks, cycle detection, _propagate_pure_ineligibility), pure_replay_progress.py (witness, shell, validate, classify and the state-write helpers), pure_replay_runtime.py (PureReplayRuntime, plus validate_frame_entry), pure_replay_executor.py (executor glue).
- Executor and recorder: OutcomeRecorder.persist_step_result(eligible_pure_settlement=) settles the exact shell on success, keeps the full result in memory and gives the summary emitter the shell; failures settle the full row. The step loop opens the single visit and cursor atomically for eligible nodes and does not increment visits twice. The pure-projection step skips all bundle I/O for derived nodes. On resume it audits conflicting surfaces and progress before the prologue, then rebuilds the required pure values into the in-memory state after the one restart-boundary determination. Failures are reported as pure_result_replay_unavailable with context.reason.
- Resume planning: determine_restart_node_id is now called once per resume, and determine_default_resume_decision takes restart_node_id=.
- Provider observation manager: created at the start of execute() and closed once at the end, not at construction. I changed two existing assertions in tests/test_provider_observation_workflow.py that asserted construction-time creation, because the spec reverses that.
- Checkpoints: emit_runtime_shadow_record emits nothing for eligible pure steps. capture_restore_payload drops bindings sourced from them. Default resume filters eligible pure points before nearest-boundary selection. The nearest-prior-boundary block was extracted into _prior_boundary_decision. The zero-record case returns VALIDATED_FRAME_ENTRY_REPLAY, and fails closed with lexical_default_resume_prior_boundary_not_restorable when validation fails.
- Docs: specs/state.md section 'Derived Pure-Result Persistence Profile'. Tests: tests/test_derived_pure_replay_profile.py (16 behavioural tests).

VERIFICATION
- Full suite: 139 failures. Re-running those files on a stashed baseline gave 138 of the same failures (provider isolation, docker, nanobragg, tmux, AF_UNIX path-length environment issues). The one extra, test_watchdog_orc_resume_reuses_provider_and_publishes_once, was my bug: the boundary scan missed address-form refs in guard conditions. I fixed it. A later re-run of the resume/call/checkpoint/state/supervision subset showed no failures beyond the baseline set, but I did not re-run the whole suite after the final edits.

ALTERNATIVES
- Making _determine_resume_default_resume_decision take restart_node_id as a parameter would break existing tests that monkeypatch it with (self, state); I pass the boundary through a one-shot attribute instead.
- Treating loop-owned nodes with a separate reason was dropped; they report multiple_visit_region like other multiply visited nodes.
- _propagate_pure_ineligibility makes a pure node ineligible when it depends on an ineligible pure node. This is conservative and less minimal than letting it read the durable row.

NOT COVERED / UNCERTAIN
- The spec leaves several signatures open and I guessed: the shape of a binding's path and address (a tuple path and the executable_ir address types, one per exact ref leaf), the evaluate_node callable (called with the RuntimeStep and the overlay state, returning a step-result dict), and the resolve_bundle_path argument (the node id). Hidden tests may expect different shapes.
- Not exercised by any test I wrote: call-frame profile selection through a real child call (only existing call tests pass); the run and force-restart CLI selection; checkpoint_record and restore_payload conflict detection; the clean-run 'no pure_projection checkpoint record' property on a schema-2 workflow with effects; and the resume-between-effects scenario with a committed-effect call counter.
- The VALIDATED_FRAME_ENTRY_REPLAY decision is tested only through validate_frame_entry, because the pure-projection fixture compiles to a historical-compatibility route. The existing supervision resume e2e passes through that path.
- An eligible node's skipped or pre-execution failed row gets a visit opened immediately before the row is written (begin then settle) so classification stays valid.
- Cross-frame ref rejection, reachability_ambiguous, a union transient row and the error-cause mapping (binding_unresolved, evaluation_failed, output_contract_invalid) are implemented but not covered by tests.
value.summary: Added the derived_pure_replay.v1 profile: selector and selection in RunState/StateManager/run/force-restart/fresh Workflow Lisp child frames, an eligibility and dependency index, exact value-free completion shells with atomic visit/settle methods, in-memory replay at resume, checkpoint filtering with a validated-frame-entry default-resume case, and a spec section. Most of it is tested only on a one-node workflow, and some parts are untested or only partly done (see account).
